words: A house that remembers everyone who lived in it. Survive five nights. Find out why the lights never go out.
The house learns where you hide, and stops letting you.
Batteries are rare. Darkness hides things — including you.
Rooms move. Doors lead somewhere new each time you play.
Pages found in the house. Each one you read reveals the next.
Playable — we'd suggest turning the fog quality down.
We'll write to you. From the house.
A made-up game. Contains scenes some players may find frightening. Rated 18.
Something is scratched into the last page…
Another page slides out from the binding
The door in the cellar was never locked. It was being held shut. I let go tonight. If you are reading this, please —
turn the lights off before you leave.
Scratched into the paper, over and over:
It contains fear, blood and things that move in the dark.
Each letter has moved three places along the alphabet.
We got the keys today. The estate agent wouldn't come past the gate. Lena says I'm imagining it, but the house was warm when we arrived. Nobody has lived here for thirty years.
Found a door in the cellar that isn't on the floor plans. It's locked from the other side.
The scratching starts at 3:12 every night. Always 3:12. Lena has started sleeping with the lights on.
I asked in the village about the last family. The woman at the shop crossed herself and closed early.
